subject: FinServCo - Eval setup & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@finservco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: FinServCo - Eval setup & next steps

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope and what success looks like for the evaluation on Redwood: 

Summary of needs (as I understand them)
- 3 focused use cases: account summarization, KYC form autofill, and policy-exception detection.
- Data: ~2k anonymized examples for each use case to start (CSV or JSONL ok; see format below).
- Success criteria: precision/recall targets for extraction, top-1 accuracy for summaries, and human-rated relevance >= 4/5.

Recommended evaluation plan
1) Models to include (initial sweep)
   - redwood/llama-2-13b-chat (instruction-tuned) — baseline for conversational quality
   - redwood/mistral-instruct-xl — stronger for instruction-following and extraction tasks
   - redwood/gptq-7b-q4_0 — low-cost, quantized baseline to measure cost/latency tradeoffs
2) Prompt sets: we recommend 3 prompt variants per task (concise, few-shot, constrained output schema). Attached sample_prompts.jsonl has examples you can edit.
3) Dataset format: JSONL with these fields: 
   - input: string (raw user query or document segment)
   - reference: string (gold output)
   - id: string (unique example id)
   - metadata: optional JSON string (customer_id, product, risk_flag)
   Example: {"id":"acct-001","input":"Summarize account activity for Q1...","reference":"Customer had 3 transactions...","metadata":"{\"product\":\"checking\"}"}
4) Scoring: automated + human loop
   - automated metrics: ROUGE-L for summaries, exact match / token-match for structured extraction
   - hallucination check: rule-based entity overlap (extract expected entities, check missing/extra)
   - human eval: 200 sample pairs across tasks, 1-5 relevance scale (we'll run blind evals inside Redwood Optimize)

Redwood eval setup (what I will do from our side)
- I will create an eval job in your tenant with the three models above and the 3 prompt variants.
- We'll provide an initial run with the first 500 examples per task to surface obvious regressions quickly.
- We'll publish per-model dashboards (latency, cost, token breakdown) and quality curves.

Action items / next steps
- Jordan: share anonymized JSONL for the three use cases (S3 link or Drive folder) by EOD Monday so we can start the initial run.
- Marissa (me): I'll provision the eval job and share config + scoring script; attach eval_instructions.pdf and scoring_config.yaml for reference.
- Neha: loop in solutions engineer to help with edge-case prompt templates if we see extraction gaps.

Security & compliance note
- If you need this run in an isolated environment, we can run the eval on Dedicated capacity or within your Private deployment; mention preference when you send the data. All runs are logged and we can provide audit records.

Thanks — feel free to reply with any changes to the plan. Happy to jump on a quick 30 min session if you want to review the sample prompts together.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0139
